sections.h2: Where a Carteret County deed gets filed
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds takes deeds for recording at the County Administrative Building, 302 Courthouse Square, Beaufort. The public can inspect records there on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

This office is the legal custodian of every land record and land transaction in the county, and each one is indexed and imaged into the permanent file. Only military discharges are closed to the public. An online database lets you view and print land records from home, which is the quickest way to find your vesting deed before listing.

Older paperwork works differently. Books 301 through 514 are on aperture cards, and a cancelled deed of trust is stamped on the card itself. If an old loan was released but the online image does not show it, call the office instead of assuming the lien is still open.

The county keeps a single fee list, and its real estate lines follow the statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10. The office takes cash, credit or debit card, money orders and cashier's checks for recording.

Recording fees
Document or serviceFee
General instruments other than deeds of trust and mortgages$26 covers 15 pages, then $4 a page
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64 covers 35 pages, then $4 a page
Plats$21 per sheet
Satisfaction instrumentsNo fee
Document containing multiple instrumentsAdditional $10
Nonstandard documentsAdditional $25
Certified copies$5 for page one, $2 per page after
Uncertified copies$0.25
Excise tax$2 per $1000.00 of sales price

An assignment that carries extra index references adds $10 for each one. Military discharges are recorded free. Ask the office to confirm the amounts before you write a check.

Follow the county's recording standards. A paper that falls short will still be recorded, though the office charges $25 more than the usual fee.

  • Page size: letter or legal.
  • First page: leave 3 inches blank across the top.
  • Remaining sides of page one and all sides of later pages: a 1/4 inch blank margin on the standards page.
  • Print: black on white, in a legible font, with 10 points as the smallest size treated as legible.
  • Pages: one-sided only.
  • Title: name the kind of instrument at the head of page one.

Side margins are the one point to check. The fee page says the minimum went back to one-half inch under Session Law 2019-117, while the standards page shows 1/4 inch, so ask the office which one it applies before you print the deed. Pen is acceptable for blanks and corrections, and the office may treat slightly small type as legible and skip the fee.

sections.h2: Who pays the stamp tax when a Carteret County house sells?
sections.html:
The seller does. The transferor pays the register before recording, as G.S. 105-228.30 directs.

The statutory rate is $1.00 per $500.00, rounding any remainder up to a whole unit. The county fee list shows the same thing as $2 per $1000.00 of the sales price. On a settlement statement it appears on the seller's side, since the closing agent usually withholds it from your proceeds.

Filing matters as much as the tax. Until a transfer is registered in the county where the land lies, G.S. 47-18 leaves it ineffective against lien creditors and paying purchasers. A buyer who skips recording leaves the door open to later claims.

sections.h2: What to pull from the records before listing
sections.html:
Gather four things from the online database or the Beaufort counter: your vesting deed, each deed of trust on the parcel with its release if one exists, any plat for the lot, and recorded easements. Plats are $21 a sheet on the fee list, and map copies are $1.00 or $2.00 depending on size.

  • The vesting deed shows exactly how title is held, including any co-owners who must sign.
  • A recorded satisfaction shows an old loan was released, and filing one costs nothing.
  • A plat or map shows the lot lines before a buyer's survey does.
  • Uncertified copies are $0.25 a page, so printing the record for your own file is cheap.

A recorded release is the proof a title company looks for. Paid-off loan with no release on file? Have the lender record one now, before the buyer's title search turns up the gap.

Taxes still open on the parcel come out of the closing. Phone the Tax Administration Office at 252-728-8485 early to get the amount. That office is in the same Beaufort building, so you can do both errands in one visit.

The two offices do different jobs. The register files the deed and takes in the stamp tax. The tax office bills the annual tax, answers value questions and tracks relief claims. Due dates, interest, appeals and collection are laid out in the Carteret County property tax guide.

The office also holds birth, death and marriage records for events within the county, and it issues certified copies. Certified death certificates and marriage license copies cost $10 each. Not everyone is eligible for a certified copy, so check before you go.

An heir selling a parent's house would normally collect the death certificate, the vesting deed and certified copies of recorded papers touching the land. Certified copies of recorded papers run $5 for page one, then $2 a page. With an estate involved, the Carteret County Clerk of Superior Court can say what the estate file needs.

This is a recording office. It gives no legal advice, supplies no legal forms and will not explain the legal effect of an instrument, so use an attorney for drafting.

A usual sequence for a seller: pull the vesting deed, confirm any old loan shows a release, have an attorney draft the deed to the layout standards, pay the stamp tax out of proceeds at closing, and record the deed promptly so the buyer's ownership is on the public index. Staff will not review the deed's legal effect, so any question about wording goes to your attorney before signing, not to the counter afterward.

Owners who live elsewhere can mail documents to the Beaufort address above and check the record remotely through the online database.

sections.h2: Carteret County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Population reached 70,469 on July 1, 2025, a 4.1% rise over 2020, spread across 54,293 housing units. The median owned home was worth $333,300 for 2020-2024, and owners occupy 74.7% of units.

With that many units, the recorded history on an older parcel can be long. Read the chain of deeds and any aperture card notes before a buyer's title company does.

faqs.q: Will Carteret County charge me to file a release after I pay off my mortgage?
faqs.a: No. Releases of paid-off loans are recorded free under the statute.

faqs.q: What does a standard Carteret County deed cost to file?
faqs.a: A standard deed is $26 for up to 15 pages, with $4 for each page added. A deed that breaks the layout standards adds $25, and a document that bundles several instruments adds $10.

faqs.q: How can I pay for recording at the Carteret County register of deeds?
faqs.a: Cash, a card, a money order or a cashier's check all work. Mail can be sent to 302 Courthouse Square, Beaufort, NC 28516.

faqs.q: Can I view Carteret County deeds online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the Register of Deeds Online Database, where land records can be viewed and printed. Books 301 through 514 are on aperture cards, so call the office about cancellation details for those older records.

faqs.q: What is the Carteret County transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: The seller pays $2 per $1000.00 of the sales price before filing. That equals the state's $1.00 per $500.00.
